body.heading: Five hot seconds
paragraphs: A message stings, a comment lands wrong, and your reply is typed before your judgment arrives. The first response is usually written by the feeling, not by you — and feelings are poor editors.
A pause does not suppress the feeling. It gives the rest of you time to show up: the part that knows the relationship matters more than the point.

body.heading: Making the pause real
paragraphs: For messages: read it twice, and if your chest is tight, wait an hour. Almost nothing that feels urgent actually is. For conversations: a breath, a sip of water, and 'Let me think about that' buys you all the time you need.
You will still sometimes say the sharp thing. But the ratio changes, and relationships are built — or worn down — on ratios.

description: Most regretted words were spoken in the first five seconds. A short pause is the cheapest communication upgrade there is.
